title: Draft how much the player can carry in each phase of the game
tier_reason: The keep line is economy tuning, which is a designer ruling and not an engineering constant.
ask: Accepted “What harvest-as-seed costs us in the simulation, honestly”. The keep line is economy tuning, which is a designer ruling and not an engineering constant.
first_action: Draft a decision card proposing the on-person carry limit for early game (Daniel suggested 5 or 10) and the increments each storage tier adds, with a recommendation, framed against how many plantings a player needs in hand to never stall.
source_message: Accepted “What harvest-as-seed costs us in the simulation, honestly”.
result:
Q-113 is drafted and staged: a decision card in `hq/data/decisions/Q-113.json`, with the matching entry in `docs/DESIGNER_QUEUE.md`. It proposes 10 crops on her person for early game and 40 at a future grain silo, against a low option of 5 and a no-cap-yet option, and recommends the 10/40 split.

I checked it against the actual game rather than taking it on faith: there's no carry cap in the sim today at all — a harvested crop goes straight into an uncapped count, so this is a genuinely new limit, not a tweak to an existing one. The 10 is sized so she can harvest-and-replant her entire starter plot (about nine tiles) in one sitting without ever being told no for a reason the screen doesn't explain — the same failure a real play session already hit 17 times in 27 actions. The 40 is sized against a fully worked wheat farm (10–12 tiles), so it only ever bites when she's stockpiling on purpose. Pricing for the silo (80–100g) is pegged to the sprinkler, the last shop item that costs gold and adds no new work.

One thing flagged inside the card rather than settled by it: today a planted seed makes exactly one harvested crop back, so a farm that replants itself has no surplus for this cap to ever apply to. That's a separate, still-open question about whether a planting should yield more than it cost — I left it filed rather than deciding it here, since it's its own ruling.

This needs your call between the three options before the sim work can start on the cap.

Complete: the card is fully drafted, staged, uncommitted in this worktree. Nothing pushed — house rules for this session have me leave it for the chief of staff to review and land.

recommend: the choice is 5 vs 10 vs no cap yet for the on-person limit (and 40 for the silo). I recommend 10/40 — it's the only option where nothing in her first sitting ever hits the ceiling, which is the whole point of a soft economy for a pre-reader. The alternative you might reasonably prefer is "no cap until the silo exists" (option c) — it's simpler to build and removes all friction, but it also means the shipping bin never gets a reason to matter in phase 1 at all, which was the reason this change was asked for.

diff.why_not: the patch no longer applies — docs/DESIGNER_QUEUE.md, hq/data/decisions/Q-113.json have changed since it was written

check.summary: The card does what the item asked (10 on her person, 40 at the silo, against 5 and no-cap, with a recommendation), but it misquotes the evidence it leans on, miscounts the starter plot, and files a second copy of a yield question Marcus already filed and escalated on the sibling item — rule the yield question first or together, since a cap of any size is moot while one seed gives back one crop.

findings.what: Evidence misquoted: the record is '17 of the session's 27 refusals gave no reason' (well and bin taps with nothing to do), not '17 unexplained refusals out of 27 actions'; the card and the queue entry both use the wrong denominator
findings.fix: Reword both to '17 of a session's 27 refusals gave no reason' and drop 'actions'

findings.what: Starter plot miscounted: the inherited row is five tiles (13–17 on row 4; 12,4 is where the neighbour stands), plus three behind it, eight in all — so 'a cap of 5 runs out before she has replanted even that first row' is false; the 5-vs-10 case still holds on the eight-tile plot
findings.fix: Say 'a row of five plus three behind, eight in all' and re-hang the argument on the whole plot, not the first row

findings.what: The yield-vs-cost follow-up is a duplicate: Marcus's own sibling item already carries 'File the harvest-as-seed economy question for a ruling' (owner marcus) and escalated the same question to Daniel; this reply assigns a second copy to milo while the queue text says 'filed to me'
findings.fix: Drop the milo follow-up, point the queue entry at the one already filed, and make owner and text agree

findings.what: Both links are dead ends: the harvest-as-seed sim analysis is the result of work item wfa0d0918389 and does not live in DESIGNER_QUEUE.md, and Q-11's soft-floor ruling is in docs/M1_PLAN.md, yet both hrefs point at the top of DESIGNER_QUEUE.md
findings.fix: Link Q-11 to docs/M1_PLAN.md and the sim analysis to its work item or a section anchor

findings.what: The recommended pick is written into the option label as '(Recommended)' instead of the `recommended: true` flag HQ renders from
findings.fix: Add "recommended": true to option b and remove the suffix from the label, as Q-112 does

findings.what: Reply overclaims 'I checked it against the actual game': the 10–12 tile wheat-farm ceiling, the 30–40 silo range and the 80–100g price are carried over from Marcus's earlier arithmetic on the sibling item, not measured; the card also calls the sprinkler a thing that 'does no new work', though it waters
findings.fix: Label the farm ceiling as an estimate from the day's action budget, and say 'adds no new verb' rather than 'does no new work'
